get.description: Search and filter procurement notices. Every parameter is optional, so filters can stand alone without a keyword. Results are ranked by relevance unless `sort` is set, and paginated with `next_cursor`.

parameters.description: Free-text keyword search over the notice (each 2–500 characters). Repeatable; multiple values are combined per `query_operator`.

parameters.description: How multiple `query` keywords combine: match all (`and`) or any (`or`). Default `or`.

parameters.description: Filter to notices in these ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 countries. Repeatable.

parameters.name: cpv_code
parameters.description: Filter to notices classified under these CPV codes. Repeatable.

parameters.name: buyer_id
parameters.description: Filter to notices involving these buyers (by id). Repeatable.

parameters.name: supplier_id
parameters.description: Filter to notices awarded to these suppliers (by id). Repeatable.

parameters.name: stage

x-enumDescriptions.stale_pre_tender: A pre-tender notice that has aged well past the point where a tender would normally have followed. Treat it as unlikely to progress.

x-enumDescriptions.closed_tender: The submission deadline has passed and the buyer has not published an award yet.
x-enumDescriptions.canceled_tender: The buyer withdrew or abandoned the procurement before awarding it.
x-enumDescriptions.unknown_tender: A tender notice whose deadline could not be determined from the source, so we can't say whether it is still open.

x-enumDescriptions.exclude_framework_agreements: Everything except the notices that establish a framework — keeps call-offs and non-framework procurements.

info.title: Stotles Public API
info.description:
The Stotles Public API gives you programmatic access to UK public sector procurement
data — notices, buyers, suppliers and framework agreements — as JSON over HTTPS.

## Base URL

All endpoints live under a versioned path:

```
https://api.stotles.com/v1
```

## Authentication

Every request needs an API key, sent in the `x-api-key` header:

```bash
curl -G https://api.stotles.com/v1/notices/search \
  -H "x-api-key: $STOTLES_API_KEY" \
  --data-urlencode "query=cyber security"
```

Keys are issued by Stotles — ask your Customer Success Manager. A key identifies
your organization, so treat it as a secret: keep it server-side and out of source
control.

Requests without a valid key get a `401`.

## Rate limits

Each API key may make **1,000 requests per hour**, and no more than
**3 requests per second**. Both apply at once, so a burst of parallel
requests can be throttled well inside your hourly allowance.

Over either limit you get a `429` carrying a `Retry-After` header — the number of
seconds to wait. Honour it and retry; a client that retries immediately will keep
getting `429`s. If these limits don't fit your use case, talk to your Customer
Success Manager.

## Pagination

List endpoints (`/search`) return an `items` array plus a top-level
`next_cursor`:

```json
{ "items": [ … ], "next_cursor": "eyJwYWdlIjoyLCJsaW1pdCI6MjB9" }
```

To read the next page, pass that value back as `?cursor=…`. Keep going until
`next_cursor` is `null`, which means you have reached the last page.

Two things to get right:

- **A short page is not the last page.** A page can contain fewer than `limit`
  items and still have more results behind it. Only `next_cursor: null` ends the
  loop.
- **Cursors are opaque.** Pass them back byte-for-byte. Don't decode, construct or
  persist them — the encoding is an implementation detail and may change.

## Errors

Errors use [RFC 9457 problem details](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9457) with
the `application/problem+json` content type:

```json
{
  "type": "https://api.stotles.com/problems/validation",
  "title": "Request validation failed",
  "status": 400,
  "detail": "The request parameters failed validation. See the 'errors' array for details.",
  "errors": [{ "parameter": "limit", "detail": "Too big: expected number to be <=50" }]
}
```

- **Branch on `type`**, not on `title` or `detail` — `type` is a stable
  identifier per error category; the human-readable fields may be reworded.
- On validation failures, `errors[]` locates each problem: `parameter` for a
  query or path parameter, `pointer` for a request body field, `header` for a
  header.

## Conventions

- **Field names and query parameters are `snake_case`.**
- **Identifiers are UUIDs.** The `id` a resource returns is the same `id` you
  filter by (`buyer_id`, `supplier_id`, `framework_id`).
- **Dates are calendar dates**, `YYYY-MM-DD`, never timestamps. There is no
  meaningful empty date, so an unknown date is `null`.
- **Money is a decimal amount plus a currency** — `{ "amount": 4500000, "currency": "GBP" }`
  — not integer minor units. Amounts can be large and are estimates, so parse them
  with a big-decimal type rather than a float. `currency` can be `null` when the
  source didn't state one.
- **Country codes are ISO 3166-1 alpha-2** (`GB`, `IE`).
- **Multi-value filters repeat the parameter**: `?stage=open_tender&stage=closed_tender`
  matches either. Don't comma-join values.
- **Range filters carry an explicit operator suffix** — `publish_date_gte`,
  `value_lte`. Both bounds are inclusive.
- **Unknown optional text is an empty string** where blank is meaningful, and
  `null` where absence is meaningful. Each field's description says which.

## Versioning and stability

The version is in the path (`/v1`). Within a version we make only additive
changes — new endpoints, new optional parameters, new response fields — so **write
clients that ignore fields they don't recognize**. Anything breaking (removing or
renaming a field, changing a type, tightening validation) goes in a new version,
and we will contact you before retiring one.

## Support

For questions, bug reports, or requests for data we don't expose yet, contact your
Stotles Customer Success Manager.
